passages.note: Official bill-details page names Smaltz as HB 1032's author; it also reports a later Senate defeat, which is not his own act.

passages.provision_quote: (b) The general assembly may amend the congressional districts
passages.note: Bill text printed under Smaltz's name lets the general assembly itself amend congressional maps off-cycle and channels any apportionment challenge to exclusive, stayed Supreme Court review rather than stating a partisan-bias standard.
passages.actor_quote: Smaltz December 1, 2025, read first time and referred to Committee on Elections and Apportionment.

passages.note: Smaltz voted Yea as HB 1032 passed the House 57-41 on third reading.

rows.reasoning: As HB 1032's author and a Yea vote on its House third-reading passage, Smaltz backed letting '(b) The general assembly may amend the congressional districts' itself rather than an independent commission, matching the legislature-draws clause shared by rungs 4 and 5. But the bill's own court provisions preserve 'mandatory and exclusive jurisdiction' for the state supreme court over apportionment appeals (only staying and prioritizing them) without stating a partisan-bias standard, so the evidence shows the legislature-controls direction without separating 'state legislatures with court oversight to prevent extreme partisan bias' from 'the party that controls the state legislature without outside interference.'
